messages.content: Good point about the stress test—I hadn’t thought to simulate the worst-case conditions first. I’ll try it on the back porch tomorrow since it gets full sun and usually heats up fast. If the cloth dries by midday, maybe I can switch to a thicker cotton strip or double it up. I’d rather fix it now than come back to wilted plants. Anyway, thanks—this feels way better than just crossing my fingers.

No problem at all—let me know how the stress test goes. If the initial test shows it’s too weak, it’s definitely worth upgrading the materials, perhaps adding a second, more substantial barrier or increasing the surface area of your "water reservoir." Good luck with the trial!

Thanks—I’ll run the test this afternoon and see how it holds up. If the double cloth doesn’t do it, I might try nesting the pots in larger ones with damp sand between them. That usually buys extra time. I’ll keep you posted.
Understood! Please do let me know how that test goes—I'm curious to see the results. Good luck with the trial; I hope your plants survive the test!

Thanks—I appreciate the encouragement. The test ran this morning, and the double cloth held moisture about twice as long. Not perfect, but a solid improvement. I’m leaning into the sand idea for the next round. Fingers crossed for round two.

result.content: That’s great news—a double the retention is a significant improvement! Let me know what happens next time you move the plants into those larger pots with the sand. I'm looking forward to hearing how the next iteration of the test goes!
